overview: The committee discussed the initial rezoning process for the Boston Avenue corridor and the Tufts Institutional District, focusing on defining geographic boundaries and land use. The committee also explored implementing 40R 'Smart Growth' zoning overlays to secure state financial incentives for the city's high school building project.

items.title: Presentation on Boston Avenue and Tufts Institutional District Rezoning
items.summary: Consultants from Innes Land Strategies Group presented existing zoning, land use, and ownership maps to initiate the rezoning process for the Tufts University area and Boston Avenue.

items.title: Discussion of Rezoning Boundaries and District Scope
items.summary: The committee considered narrowing the project scope to focus on the northern Hillside neighborhood section of Boston Avenue while deferring the southern Ball Square section to a later phase. Members discussed removing purely residential parcels from the study area to align with executive policy directives.

items.title: Impact of Dover Amendment and Campus Zoning
items.summary: Director of Planning, Development, and Sustainability Alicia Hunt explained how the Dover Amendment limits the city's authority over institutional development and argued that current residential zoning does not appropriately regulate campus buildings. The committee discussed creating campus-specific zoning to better manage building heights and setbacks.

items.title: Evaluation of 40R and 40S Smart Growth Zoning
items.summary: The committee reviewed the potential for 40R zoning overlays, which could unlock $8 million to $12 million in state reimbursements for the new high school by incentivizing affordable housing. Staff recommended fast-tracking a 40R application for Medford Square to meet state deadlines for the school project.

items.title: Public Comment and Committee Motions
items.summary: The committee requested that the consultants return with revised boundaries for the Hillside section of Boston Avenue and directed the Planning department to begin separate work on a 40R strategy for Medford Square. A resident expressed concerns regarding the scale of university development and the impact of institutional zoning on adjacent residential properties.
